I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou, this is the crop pattern I trust most because the machinery, irrigation, and selling channels all match it, and at my age I care more about a steady harvest than chasing a risky higher return. I already know how to manage wheat and maize well enough without making the year too complicated, and this rotation also fits our water and labor conditions better than switching into something like cotton or vegetables on a larger scale.

For wheat, I will hold the stand through spring, topdress nitrogen in stages, water at the key points, and keep disease control simple and timely. After wheat harvest, I will return the straw, get the summer maize in quickly, use improved seed, apply fertilizer in a moderate way, irrigate only when the crop really needs it, and do pest control mainly around the common pressure periods. I will use ploughing ahead of wheat because I want the straw incorporated well and the soil loosened, then use rotary tillage ahead of maize so I can turn the field around fast after wheat harvest. I am choosing a conservative, familiar plan because it gives me the best balance of yield, cost control, and manageability.
